description: Terraform Cloud / HCP Terraform CI OIDC tokens against Azure Entra FLEXIBLE federated-identity-credential expressions (azure-fic-flexible) -- PREVIEW. Third and final issuer Microsoft supports for flexible FIC (after GitHub and GitLab); zero matcher changes. The TFC sub is a name-based path plus the run phase: organization:{org}:project:{project}:workspace:{workspace}:run_phase:{plan|apply}, minted by the issuer https://app.terraform.io. run_phase is the case flexible FIC exists for: because classic FIC is a direct string match, 'two federated identity credentials need to be created for each workspace using dynamic credentials: one that matches run_phase:plan and one that matches run_phase:apply' -- flexible FIC collapses that pair into one matches expression, which also collapses the plan/apply trust separation. Like GitLab, TFC flexible FIC references ONLY sub; the immutable terraform_organization_id / terraform_project_id / terraform_workspace_id are SEPARATE claims it cannot reference, and TFC exposes no sub customization, so -- unlike GitLab's project_id-led sub -- there is NO policy-side lever to pin an immutable id. matches semantics: ? one character, * multiple, anchored, not path-aware (spans ':').

vectors.description: The tightest pin: claims['sub'] eq the fully-qualified workspace path at the apply phase. eq is exact, so it admits exactly one workspace's apply runs -- but on the mutable name path (organization/project/workspace names), with no immutable id available.
vectors.subject: organization:my-org:project:my-project:workspace:my-workspace:run_phase:apply

judgment.reason: eq admits exactly this workspace's apply phase -- the correct scope for a write-capable role -- but the sub is entirely name-based (organization/project/workspace names), so a rename changes it and there is no immutable id to fall back on: TFC flexible FIC references only sub, and the immutable terraform_*_id claims are not addressable. Durable within a stable naming scheme; fragile across renames.

vectors.description: The marquee flexible-FIC case, and its trap. Classic FIC needs two credentials per workspace -- 'one that matches run_phase:plan and one that matches run_phase:apply' -- so admins reach for flexible FIC to collapse them into claims['sub'] matches '...:run_phase:*'. The same wildcard that removes the two-credential chore also removes the plan/apply separation: this credential is assumable during the PLAN phase (matched here by a run_phase:plan token), not just apply.
vectors.subject: organization:my-org:project:my-project:workspace:my-workspace:run_phase:plan

judgment.reason: run_phase:* trusts both phases in one credential. HashiCorp keeps them as SEPARATE credentials precisely because they are distinct trust levels -- plan runs earlier in the run lifecycle than the approved apply -- so a write-capable role behind a run_phase:* credential becomes assumable during plan, which the per-phase split exists to prevent. Pin run_phase to apply with eq for write roles; use a plan-scoped, read-only role for plan.

vectors.description: A wildcard at the workspace segment: claims['sub'] matches 'organization:my-org:project:my-project:workspace:*:run_phase:apply' admits the apply phase of ANY workspace in the project (matched here by a different workspace). Wildcarding the workspace segment is how a TFC trust is broadened from one workspace to a whole project in a single credential -- the anchored matches * consumes the workspace name.
vectors.subject: organization:my-org:project:my-project:workspace:other-workspace:run_phase:apply

judgment.reason: Every workspace in the project -- including workspaces created after the credential -- can assume the identity on apply. Convenient for a fleet, but it grants each workspace whatever this credential's role holds, defeating per-workspace isolation. Scope to the named workspace, or use per-workspace credentials.

vectors.description: The broadest form: claims['sub'] matches 'organization:my-org:*' admits every project, workspace, and run phase in the organization, because matches `*` is not path-aware and spans the ':' separators. The exact string classic FIC would treat as an inert literal; flexible FIC HONORS it. Matched here by an apply run of an unrelated project/workspace.
vectors.subject: organization:my-org:project:finance:workspace:prod-db:run_phase:apply

judgment.reason: Organization-wide trust: any project, any workspace, and BOTH run phases assume the identity, and new projects/workspaces inherit it immediately. This is the maximal collapse -- it drops the workspace, project, AND run_phase scoping at once. Pin at least the project and workspace, and the run phase.

vectors.description: The TFC immutable-id dead end. The token carries immutable ids (terraform_workspace_id here, plus terraform_project_id / terraform_organization_id) as SEPARATE claims, but TFC flexible FIC references only sub, and the sub is name-based with no customization option. So a workspace deleted and recreated under the same organization/project/workspace name mints a byte-identical sub -- a different terraform_workspace_id the credential cannot see -- and an exact eq admits it. The sub is the only lever, and it carries no immutable id.
vectors.subject: organization:my-org:project:my-project:workspace:my-workspace:run_phase:apply

judgment.reason: The sub is name-based and TFC exposes no id-based sub, so the immutable terraform_workspace_id (a fresh id on the recreated workspace here) is unreachable by a sub-only flexible-FIC expression -- there is no policy-side lever to pin it. Narrower than a public path-reuse (recreating a workspace under the same name needs organization/project create permission), but structurally unfixable at the trust policy: whoever can recreate the name inherits the trust, and a rename silently breaks it. Govern workspace naming/lifecycle as part of the trust boundary.

vectors.description: The mechanical basis the run_phase:* trap rides on: an exact claims['sub'] eq '...:run_phase:apply' does NOT match a run_phase:plan token. plan and apply are distinct subject strings, which is exactly why classic FIC needs one credential per phase -- and why the run_phase:* wildcard (sibling tfc-flex-run-phase-wildcard-collapses-plan-apply) is a real widening, not a formality.
vectors.subject: organization:my-org:project:my-project:workspace:my-workspace:run_phase:plan
